A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same VIBE research paper and complete Appendices A–K. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that all substantive content matches; visible differences are confined to the first-page arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original VIBE experiments against backdoor attacks, including benchmark ACC/ASR results, combined attacks, ablations, and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 contains the same original benchmark experiments and appendix analyses, including the VIBE comparisons in Tables 1–9 and sensitivity results in Tables 10–16.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain identical EM updates, posterior parameterizations, self-supervised initialization, and manifold-based preprocessing. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-30, and ImageNet-1k with identical attack coverage, including clean-label, combined, adaptive, and self-supervision attacks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in every corresponding experiment. Table 1 retains ABL, DBD, CBD, ASD, and VaB; transfer-learning and appendix comparisons also retain their respective baseline sets.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices G–J report identical poisoning rates, metrics, model configurations, sample counts, training budgets, and evaluation procedures. No existing setting is revised or new protocol introduced.

E4.justification: The poisoning-rate and feature-extractor analyses, preprocessing ablations, adaptive-attack tests, hyperparameter sweeps, and latent-space visualizations are unchanged across Section 6 and Appendices I–K.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the statement that results are averaged over three runs and variance does not exceed 0.2%. Run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged throughout both PDFs.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match, including appendix results. For example, Table 1 retains CIFAR-10 VIBE-SS-F averages of 94.3% ACC and 3.2% ASR.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, ELBO and optimal-transport formulations, posterior derivations, and adaptive-attack objective are identical. Equations 1–38 and the derivations in Appendices A–E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about latent-label recovery, model-agnostic backdoor defense, and effectiveness against adaptive and combined attacks.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications remain identical, including initialization dependence, possible removal of clean samples during preprocessing, and the reproduction difficulties and storage sensitivity discussed in Appendix I.2.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information, attack configurations, and implementation links are unchanged in the main text and Appendices G–I. No code or data access instructions change.

R1.justification: Section 2, citation placements, and all 108 references are unchanged. The positioning relative to heuristic defenses, representation learning, and latent-variable models is identical.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, 11 Mar 2025 to v2, 26 Jun 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology, and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page marginal arXiv stamp is slightly repositioned. Figures 1–9, Tables 1–16, captions, and all other page layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: The main paper and Appendices A–K retain identical methods, evidence, explanations, and limitations. Updating and slightly repositioning the arXiv stamp does not meaningfully alter scientific rigor, reproducibility, or readability.
